title: Larissa: Name Meaning, Origin & Personality
summary: Larissa is a timeless and graceful feminine name with deep historical roots and a warm, inviting sound. It bridges classical antiquity and modern elegance effortlessly.
meaning: Citadel, cheerful, or place of seagulls
origin: The exact etymology of Larissa is debated by historians and linguists, adding an air of mystery to its rich history. Its origins most likely trace back to ancient Greek geography, originally referring to an ancient city and fortress, which translates to citadel or stronghold. Alternatively, some linguistic theories connect it to the ancient Greek word for a sea-gull, or suggest links to a mythological nymph. The name gained early prominence through an ancient city in Thessaly and has since spread gracefully across Eastern Europe, Russia, and the Americas, beloved for its melodic syllables.
personality: People bearing the name Larissa are often perceived as naturally creative, intuitive, and deeply compassionate. There is a quiet strength associated with the name, reflecting its historical connection to fortresses and protection, yet it carries an inherently gentle and artistic spirit. Larissas are frequently viewed as dependable friends who bring warmth and harmony to social circles. They often possess a balanced perspective, combining practical intelligence with a vivid imagination, making them thoughtful listeners and inspiring leaders who naturally uplift those around them with positivity and grace.
popularity: Larissa enjoys steady popularity across various global regions, particularly in European countries and parts of South America. While it is rarely found at the absolute peak of modern naming charts, its enduring appeal ensures it remains a familiar and well-loved choice. Parents continue to choose Larissa for its international versatility, classic charm, and the way it sounds both sophisticated and approachable across multiple languages and cultures.

faq.q: Is Larissa a modern or traditional name?
faq.ans: Larissa is a traditional name with ancient Greek roots that has been used for centuries. Despite its long history, it retains a fresh and contemporary feel today.

faq.q: How do you pronounce the name Larissa?
faq.ans: The most common pronunciation in English is luh-RIS-uh, though some regions and languages emphasize the first syllable or soften the middle consonants slightly.

faq.q: Does Larissa have any mythological connections?
faq.ans: Yes, in Greek mythology, Larissa was the name of a nymph, daughter of Pelasgus, who was associated with the ancient city of the same name.

faq.q: What are some common variations of Larissa?
faq.ans: Common variants of the name include Larysa in Ukrainian and Polish, Larisa in Russian, and the short form Lara across many different languages.
